method: Blocking: same recorded country and a shared Soundex code on any distinctive name word, or the same tax ID in any country; a record whose phone dialling code points to another country is also compared in that country. Score: the live intake scorer (src/lib/engine/dedupe.ts, ported 1:1 to Python and parity-tested): max(Jaro-Winkler, token-set ratio) on the normalised name (lowercase, punctuation and legal suffixes removed, abbreviations expanded), capped by how much of the distinctive wording both names share; the same tax ID lifts it to 0.97; same postcode, phone or company email domain add 0.03 each. Matches are grouped into golden IDs (transitive). Blocking design and threshold (0.905, the middle of the F1-best range) were chosen on SG+MY only, then frozen and scored once on TH/VN/MM. The duplicates were generated with typos, word reorder, romanisation, blank tax IDs and other address formats that the normaliser does not know about.

perPerturbation.label: Blank tax ID on the duplicate

examples.why: The distinctive words are romanised differently (Chao/Jao, Phraya/Praya), so only 'rim' matches on both sides. Name scored 0.69; same postcode, phone number and email domain added +0.09, so the total (0.78) stayed under the 0.905 threshold.

b.cardName: Bệnh viện Quốc tế Sông Sen

examples.why: One record is booked under SG, but its +84 phone number put it next to the VN record, so the pair was compared. The names are a translation, not a spelling variant ('quoc te' means 'International'), and the normaliser does not translate, so only 'song sen' matches on both sides. Name scored 0.44; same postcode, phone number and email domain added +0.09, so the total (0.53) stayed under the 0.905 threshold.

Different organisations with the same distinctive name, differing only by facility word (clinic vs hospital). Facility words are deliberately treated as generic so 'Hosp' vs 'Hospital' still matches, which makes a hospital and a clinic of the same name look alike. Score 0.93.

country + Soundex of any distinctive word
any distinctive word + dialling-code country check (chosen)

notes: 13 of 15 held-out duplicate pairs found; 1 of 14 warnings was a false alarm.
Small sample: one pair moves recall by about 7 points on the held-out countries.
Merging duplicate records alone does not change any country x product total; only records booked under the wrong country or product do.
